PAPERS.title: Vitamin D and Particulate Matter-Associated Immune Responses in People Living with HIV: A Randomized Trial with Exploratory DNA Methylation Analyses.
PAPERS.short: Wuhan PLWH vitamin D RCT PM1 PM2.5 PM10 CD4 CD19 DNA methylation mediation 2023
PAPERS.pm: PM1, PM2.5 and PM10 averaged over 72 h before each visit (source not stated in abstract)
PAPERS.endpoint: CD4+ T and CD19+ B cell counts; cytokines; CpG methylation
PAPERS.affil: Yangzhou University, China; Yangzhou University, China
PAPERS.n: Double-blind placebo-controlled trial of daily vitamin D in 80 people living with HIV (75 analysed, 271 follow-ups, March-July 2023), PM averaged over the 72 h before each 28-day visit. Supplementation attenuated the negative PM-cell count associations: the PM-associated change in CD4+ T cells differed from placebo by 3.37%, 2.21% and 1.96% per 10 ug/m3 PM1, PM2.5 and PM10, and in CD19+ B cells by 4.71%, 2.98% and 2.65%. 173 vitamin D-related CpG sites changed; 25 mediated 28-79% of effects on TLR4, IL-6 and TNF-alpha. No CIs for the between-arm differences are given, randomisation is to vitamin D not to PM, and the exposure source is unstated; the PM contrast is observational within a small trial. Relevance: indirect - a short-window effect modifier study whose exposure assignment is exactly where a home sensor would sharpen it.

PAPERS.title: Retinoic Acid Alleviates Accelerated Atherosclerosis in Diesel Exhaust-Derived PM2.5-Exposed ApoE-/- Mice by Enhancing eNOS-NO Coupling.
PAPERS.short: Wonkwang ApoE-/- diesel exhaust particle nebulisation retinoic acid eNOS BH4 atherosclerosis 8 weeks
PAPERS.pm: Diesel exhaust particles by nebulisation chamber, 8 weeks; dose not stated in abstract
PAPERS.endpoint: Lung inflammation, blood pressure, lipids, aortic wall thickening; HUVEC eNOS coupling
PAPERS.affil: Wonkwang University, Republic of Korea; Wonkwang University, Republic of Korea
PAPERS.n: Retinoic acid was nominated by connectivity mapping of COPD lung transcriptomes (GEO, 5 vs 6 donors), then tested in ApoE-/- mice nebulised with diesel exhaust particles for 8 weeks with oral all-trans retinoic acid at 1 or 5 mg/kg/day. Treatment lowered BAL CXCL1/2 and lung Muc5ac, IL-1b, IL-6 and TNF-alpha, reduced blood pressure, improved serum lipids and attenuated aortic inflammatory infiltration and wall thickening; in HUVECs it raised GTPCH-1, eNOS phosphorylation, BH4 and BH4/BH2. The abstract gives no DEP concentration, group sizes or effect sizes, and DEP is a single-source surrogate for ambient PM2.5. Relevance: indirect - mechanistic cardiovascular arm; no measurement content.

PAPERS.title: Data-Driven Calibration and Reference-Free Drift Detection for Multi-Modal Sensor Systems.
PAPERS.short: TU Delft Brussels multi-modal low-cost sensor calibration transfer DANN drift detection residual monitor
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5, PM10 and PM1 from custom multi-modal low-cost devices, with O3 and NO2
PAPERS.endpoint: Calibration error (MAE, RMSE, R2, bias) on source and transfer devices; injected-drift detection
PAPERS.affil: TU Delft, The Netherlands; TU Delft, The Netherlands
PAPERS.n: Five custom multi-modal devices at two Brussels sites (9-68 days each), reference data for only a subset. MLR, Elastic Net, random forest, gradient boosting and a domain-adversarial network (DANN) were benchmarked for O3, NO2, PM2.5 and PM10 on the source unit and transferred to other units at the same and the other site, with block-bootstrap intervals. Tree ensembles had the lowest source-device errors, but for PM10 lost their advantage over the uncalibrated sensor once transferred; DANN had the best mean Calibration Transfer Ratio, not significantly. A cross-sensor residual monitor flagged injected gradual drift in reconstructable channels (PM1, UV, T, RH, CO). Five devices and short records; drift was injected, not real ageing, and the monitor cannot localise the faulty channel. Relevance: direct - quantifies the failure of calibrate-one-deploy-many for coarse PM.

PAPERS.title: Temperature-Associated SD Card Logging Failures in PurpleAir Monitors: Findings from the Strong Heart Air Study.
PAPERS.short: Strong Heart Air Study PurpleAir SD card logging failure cold temperature WiFi Oklahoma South Dakota Arizona
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 by PurpleAir monitors, 10 co-located per site, SD-card logging without WiFi
PAPERS.endpoint: Data recovery and logging failure versus ambient temperature
PAPERS.affil: Columbia University Irving Medical Center, USA; Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health, USA
PAPERS.n: Pilot co-locations of ten PurpleAir monitors at each of three American Indian community sites in a cardiovascular cohort, logging to SD card without WiFi to keep data under community control. Data recovery was 100% in Arizona but 57% in Oklahoma and 10% in South Dakota; logging failed when ambient temperature fell to a mean (SD) of 4.4 (3.2) C and 7.7 (2.0) C. Outdoor tests suggested WiFi connection protects logging at low temperature, and 4 C cold-room tests reproduced the failure without WiFi. This is a data-completeness finding, not an accuracy evaluation; firmware and SD-card models tested are not given in the abstract. Relevance: direct - offline PurpleAir deployments in cold climates will lose winter data non-randomly, exactly when wood-smoke exposure peaks, biasing any health analysis built on them.

PAPERS.title: Long-Term Field Performance of Sensirion SEN54 and SPS30 Low-Cost Particle Sensors: Seasonal Variability and Correction Using Dew Point Deficit.
PAPERS.short: CHMI Prague Sensirion SEN54 SPS30 vs Fidas 200S 19 months dew point deficit MARS correction PM10 dust
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 and PM10 from two SEN54 and two SPS30 OPCs against a Palas Fidas 200S equivalent monitor
PAPERS.endpoint: R2 and RMSE versus equivalent monitor before and after humidity correction
PAPERS.affil: Czech Hydrometeorological Institute, Czech Republic; Czech Hydrometeorological Institute, Czech Republic
PAPERS.n: Two pairs of Sensirion OPCs (SEN54, SPS30) co-located with a Fidas 200S for 19 months. Raw agreement was far worse for PM10 (mean R2 0.50, RMSE 13.70 ug/m3) than PM2.5 (R2 0.87, RMSE 5.53 ug/m3); no unit captured mineral-dust PM10 episodes. Performance was better in the cold season and much of the seasonal variation tracked dew point deficit; MARS models with sensor PM and DPD raised PM10 to R2 0.68 (RMSE 8.25) and PM2.5 to R2 0.92 (RMSE 3.29), with particle counts helping the SPS30 further. Four sensors at one site; residual warm-season underestimation remains unexplained, and the Fidas is itself an optical equivalent rather than gravimetric. Relevance: direct - dew point deficit is a cheap, transferable humidity covariate; the PM10 dust blind spot is not fixed by it.

PAPERS.title: Software-Based Relative Humidity Compensation for Low-Cost Optical PM Sensors Using Machine Learning: A Case Study from Upper Silesia, Poland.
PAPERS.short: University of Silesia SDS011 unheated vs heated software humidity compensation polynomial SVR DNN LSTM latency
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 from an unheated SDS011 with T, RH, P, targeting a co-located heated SDS011
PAPERS.endpoint: R2, MAE, RMSE against the heated sensor; inference latency
PAPERS.affil: University of Silesia, Poland; University of Silesia, Poland
PAPERS.n: 48,860 10-min records in Upper Silesia: six ML models trained to make an unheated SDS011 plus T, RH and pressure emulate a co-located heated SDS011. Sixth-degree polynomial, SVR and dense networks reached R2 94%, MAE 1.41-1.61 and RMSE 3.69-3.79 ug/m3 for PM2.5; LSTM was worse (R2 88%, MAE 2.56, RMSE 5.33) and over 500 times slower at inference (0.1215 ms/sample). The target is another low-cost sensor, so the work reproduces the heater's behaviour, not reference-grade mass; a heated inlet also evaporates semi-volatile material, so the target is biased in its own right. Single site and sensor pair. Relevance: direct - supports static non-linear RH correction on microcontrollers, but needs validation against FEM data before it substitutes for calibration.

PAPERS.title: WSN-IoT-Based Mobile Environmental Monitoring System for Smart Cities.
PAPERS.short: Universidad del Magdalena mobile WSN-IoT node edge fog cloud PM2.5 PM10 CO2 MQTT TRL 6 Santa Marta
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 and PM10 from a mobile low-cost sensor node (sensor model not stated in abstract)
PAPERS.endpoint: System function (TRL 6) and RMSE after validation
PAPERS.affil: Universidad del Magdalena, Colombia; Universidad del Magdalena, Colombia
PAPERS.n: Engineering paper describing a mobile environmental node (precipitation, PM2.5, PM10, CO2, irradiance, T, pressure, wind) with a fixed sink, edge-fog-cloud architecture, MQTT broker and web interface with geospatial queries. Store-and-forward, integrity checks and flow control are built in; laboratory and field tests reached TRL 6. Metrological evaluation against independent validation reduced RMSE for four of six variables, most for PM2.5, but no numbers are given in the abstract. No sensor model, reference instrument, duration or mobile-sampling design is reported, so the PM data quality cannot be judged from the abstract. Relevance: direct but thin - an architecture template for mobile low-cost PM mapping, without the calibration evidence needed to use its data.

PAPERS.title: Association Between Ambient PM2.5 Exposure and Leukocyte Telomere Length Among Rural Adults: Cross-Sectional Study in Northern Thailand.
PAPERS.short: Chiang Mai rural adults biomass burning PM2.5 lag 0-90 d leukocyte telomere length 8-OHdG wild cluster bootstrap
PAPERS.pm: Ambient PM2.5 cumulative averages over lag 0-7 to 0-90 days (source not stated in abstract)
PAPERS.endpoint: Relative leukocyte telomere length (qPCR T/S); 8-OHdG, SII, SIRI
PAPERS.affil: Chiang Mai University, Thailand; Chiang Mai University, Thailand
PAPERS.n: 179 rural adults in biomass-burning northern Thailand; PM2.5 averaged over five windows up to the blood draw. Positive associations with telomere length appeared only for the 0-30, 0-60 and 0-90 day windows: per window-specific IQR (8.13 and 7.25 ug/m3) relative LTL was 0.050 T/S higher (95% CI 0.012-0.089) at 0-30 days and 0.079 (0.035-0.123) at 0-60 days. Crucially, the authors' own wild cluster bootstrap over eight site-date groups left none of the five associations significant (p 0.247-0.787); the standard errors ignore site-date clustering, and p-values are unadjusted. Longer telomeres with more PM run against the usual hypothesis. Relevance: indirect - exposure varies by only eight site-date clusters, so the effective sample is eight; personal or sensor-resolved exposure is what this design lacks.

PAPERS.title: Colon Effects of 7-Day Whole-Body Inhalation Exposure of Fischer 344 Rats to Emissions from First- and Second-Generation Biodiesel Fuels with and Without a Particle Filter.
PAPERS.short: Warsaw Fischer 344 rats 7-day whole-body biodiesel exhaust B7 SHB20 DPF colon oxidative stress
PAPERS.pm: Diesel engine exhaust from B7 and SHB20 biofuels, measured PM 2.13-2.19 mg/m3 without and 0.17-0.19 mg/m3 with DPF
PAPERS.endpoint: Colon lipid peroxidation, redox and antioxidant markers, inflammation
PAPERS.affil: Warsaw University of Life Sciences, Poland; Institute of Nuclear Chemistry and Technology, Poland
PAPERS.n: Male Fischer 344 rats breathed whole-body diesel exhaust from first-generation B7 or second-generation SHB20 (FAME plus hydrotreated vegetable oil) blends for 7 days, 6 h/day, at measured PM of 2.19 and 2.13 mg/m3 without a particle filter and 0.17 and 0.19 mg/m3 with one. Exhaust induced colonic lipid peroxidation, redox shifts, antioxidant mobilisation and inflammation-associated responses; effects were blend-specific, strongest for SHB20 without DPF, and only partly mitigated by the filter. Doses are two to three orders above ambient, exposure is the whole mixture (NOx and VOCs included), and the abstract gives no effect sizes or group sizes. Relevance: indirect - the DPF arm cuts PM about 12-fold without abolishing effects, pointing at the gas phase or ultrafines that mass-based sensors do not see.

PAPERS.title: Worse than the Insult: The Role of Macrophages and Lymphocytes in Organic Dust-Induced Chronic Bronchitis.
PAPERS.short: NC A&T review organic dust livestock chronic bronchitis macrophages lymphocytes TLR4 NF-kB 18 studies
PAPERS.pm: Organic dust and its components (e.g. LPS) in livestock production
PAPERS.endpoint: Macrophage and lymphocyte activation in organic dust-associated chronic bronchitis
PAPERS.affil: North Carolina A&T State University, USA; North Carolina A&T State University, USA
PAPERS.n: Review of the cellular basis of chronic bronchitis from livestock organic dust: 25,488 database hits narrowed to 18 research articles (2015-2025). Repetitive dust or LPS exposure keeps macrophages and lymphocytes activated through TLR4, TLR2, NF-kB, PKC, ERK and MAPK signalling, sustaining cytokine and chemokine output that drives mucus hypersecretion and airway remodelling; micronutrient or anti-inflammatory co-treatment blunted inflammation in experimental work. The selection from 25,488 hits to 18 papers is not described with a reproducible protocol, no exposure-response information is extracted, and dust is characterised by source rather than size or mass. Relevance: indirect - agricultural dust is a coarse, bioactive fraction that optical low-cost sensors size poorly; no measurement content.

PAPERS.title: Comparative Susceptibility to PM2.5-Induced Pulmonary Pathology: A Lifespan-Based Perspective on Animal Models.
PAPERS.short: Chiang Mai veterinary review PM2.5 lung pathology short vs long lifespan animal models One Health sentinel
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 in laboratory rodents versus long-lived animals breathing ambient air
PAPERS.endpoint: Pulmonary phenotype by lifespan: acute reversible injury versus chronic remodelling and neoplasia
PAPERS.affil: Chiang Mai University, Thailand; Chiang Mai University, Thailand
PAPERS.n: Review contrasting PM2.5 lung disease in short-lifespan laboratory rodents, typically dosed high for a small fraction of life, with long-lived species breathing ambient air for decades. Rodents show acute, often reversible inflammation; long-lived animals show cumulative particle bioaccumulation, airway remodelling and spontaneous neoplasia. The authors concede lifespan is confounded with exposure intensity and duration and cannot be separated from them, and propose veterinary sentinel cohorts, cross-species dosimetric scaling and in-tissue particle burden measurement. No systematic search or quantitative synthesis. Relevance: indirect - sentinel-animal cohorts would need long, spatially resolved ambient exposure records, the kind dense low-cost networks can supply.

PAPERS.title: Thermally driven aerosol dynamics and ultrafine particle emissions during electric stove heating.
PAPERS.short: Penn State Soongsil electric stove hot plate ceramic pan UFP 5.08e6 cm-3 coagulation source strength decay
PAPERS.pm: Size-resolved ultrafine particle number during electric-stove heating at 250 and 540 C
PAPERS.endpoint: Peak UFP number, source strength, size distribution, loss processes
PAPERS.affil: Soongsil University, Republic of Korea; Pennsylvania State University, USA
PAPERS.n: Chamber-style tests of six electric-stove surface configurations at controller settings of 250 and 540 C, followed by decay. With no pan, total UFP reached 2.53 x 10^6 cm-3 at 250 C and 5.08 x 10^6 cm-3 at 540 C; repeated heating cut peaks by up to 91%. At 540 C the bare hot plate and a ceramic-coated pan emitted 5.47 x 10^12 and 4.89 x 10^12 particles/min in their first episodes, mostly in the smallest sizes; cookware shifted the distribution by material. Coagulation removed over 60% of early particles; deposition and ventilation dominated later, and a well-mixed model underpredicted measured concentrations. No food was cooked, so these are heater/cookware emissions only; single test space. Relevance: direct for indoor sensing - these particles are below the detection range of optical low-cost sensors, which will report a clean kitchen.

PAPERS.title: Ship emission accounting and air quality impact in Tianjin Port: Application of bottom-up method and AERMOD model.
PAPERS.short: Dalian Maritime Tianjin Port AIS bottom-up ship emission inventory AERMOD PM2.5 216.73 Mg May-July 2021
PAPERS.pm: Ship PM10 and PM2.5 emissions (AIS bottom-up) and AERMOD-dispersed ambient contributions
PAPERS.endpoint: Emissions by vessel type and mode; contribution to ambient pollutants at nearest station
PAPERS.affil: Dalian Maritime University, China; Dalian Maritime University, China
PAPERS.n: AIS-based bottom-up inventory of ship emissions at Tianjin Port for May-July 2021, dispersed with AERMOD. Ships emitted 237.97 Mg PM10 and 216.73 Mg PM2.5 alongside 1,663.85 Mg SO2 and 8,123.43 Mg NOx; conventional ships produced 40.70% of total emissions and berthing more than 32% of SO2 and 43% of NOx. At the monitoring station nearest the port ships contributed 79.13% of ambient SO2 and 58.22% of NOx but under 10% of particulate matter. Three summer months only, no model evaluation statistics in the abstract, and AERMOD omits secondary particle formation, which is how ship SO2 and NOx become PM. Relevance: indirect - port fenceline PM sensors will miss the ship signal in primary mass; SO2/NOx co-sensing is the better tracer.

PAPERS.title: Source-Space Coverage Outweighs Receptor Placement in Sparse Urban Emission Inversion Under Matched and Moderately Misspecified Transport: A Mixed Point-Road Simulation Benchmark.
PAPERS.short: Chengdu 30 synthetic cities emission inversion sensor placement vs source coverage calibration error truth-free residual
PAPERS.design: Methodological simulation with applied case study
PAPERS.pm: Pollutant-agnostic receptor network inversion; applied to seven Chengdu NO2 stations
PAPERS.endpoint: Normalised source-rate error by design decision; residual AUC for model error
PAPERS.affil: Chengdu Vocational & Technical College of Industry, China; Dalian University of Technology, China
PAPERS.n: Benchmark over 30 synthetic cities placing five network design decisions on one error scale for emission-rate inversion from concentration-mapping monitors. Under matched transport, covering traffic in the source dictionary changed normalised source error by 0.74 and dictionary fidelity and sensor calibration by about 0.68 each, versus 0.13-0.15 across placement criteria; under a mismatched dispersion generator the coverage effect fell to the size of placement. Unmodelled mixing height was among the commonest errors (0.41-0.53); a truth-free residual flagged severe model error (AUC 0.89-0.95). Applied to seven Chengdu NO2 stations, estimates were withheld for poor skill. Synthetic only; no PM application. Relevance: direct for network design - sensor calibration error outweighs siting choice by about fivefold for source inversion.

PAPERS.title: High-resolution spatiotemporal estimates of total and wildfire PM 2.5 in the contiguous United States, 2018-2024: Implications for population exposure and mortality burden
PAPERS.short: UW medRxiv CONUS 1-km daily total and wildfire PM2.5 2018-2024 ML smoke density attributable deaths
PAPERS.pm: Daily 1-km total and wildfire-specific PM2.5 from an ML model with precursors and smoke density
PAPERS.endpoint: Cross-validated R2; wildfire share of PM2.5 and of attributable deaths
PAPERS.affil: University of Washington, USA; University of Washington, USA
PAPERS.n: Preprint. ML framework estimating daily 1-km total and wildfire-attributable PM2.5 over the contiguous US for 2018-2024 from public data, including chemical precursors and smoke density. Cross-validated R2 was 0.72 daily and 0.89 annual. Wildfire smoke supplied about 35% of PM2.5 along the west coast in 2020 and over 25% in the eastern US in 2023; wildfire PM2.5 accounted for 20% of PM2.5-attributable deaths on the west coast in 2020 (30 times 2019) and 24% in the north-east in 2023 (14 times 2019). Not peer reviewed; the abstract gives no error on the wildfire component itself, the hardest part to validate, nor the concentration-response function used. Relevance: direct - a candidate exposure surface whose daily skill (R2 0.72) leaves room for PurpleAir fusion in smoke events.

PAPERS.title: Type I interferon signaling mediates silica-induced pulmonary B1 cell recruitment and autoimmunity
PAPERS.short: UCLouvain Research Square silica mice type I interferon Ifnar1 knockout B1 cells CXCL13 autoantibodies
PAPERS.pm: Crystalline silica particles instilled (dose not stated in abstract)
PAPERS.endpoint: IFN-I signature, autoantibodies, pulmonary B1-cell recruitment, CXCL13/CXCR5
PAPERS.affil: UCLouvain, Belgium; UCLouvain, Belgium
PAPERS.n: Preprint. Silica exposure produced a sustained type I interferon signature in wild-type mice with raised lung and circulating anti-dsDNA, class-switched IgG, natural IgM and IgA; these humoral changes were markedly attenuated in Ifnar1-/- mice. Silica recruited innate-like B1 cells to the lung via the CXCL13/CXCR5 axis; without IFNAR, B1 cells accumulated in tracheobronchial nodes and spleen instead and CXCL13 induction was lost. Not peer reviewed; dose, route detail, group sizes and effect sizes are absent from the abstract, and crystalline silica is an occupational particle with toxicity specific to its surface chemistry, not ambient PM. Relevance: indirect - mechanistic link from particle lung injury to systemic autoimmunity; no measurement content.

PAPERS.title: Lagged environmental effects on multi-pathogen respiratory positivity: a distributed-lag nonlinear analysis of seven Sichuan sentinel hospitals, China
PAPERS.short: Sichuan CDC seven sentinel hospitals DLNM multi-pathogen ARI positivity humidity RSV PM2.5 H. influenzae FDR
PAPERS.pm: Weekly PM2.5 among six pollutants plus temperature and humidity (source not stated in abstract)
PAPERS.endpoint: Pathogen-specific positivity among acute respiratory infection cases
PAPERS.affil: Sichuan Center for Disease Control and Prevention, China; Sichuan Center for Disease Control and Prevention, China
PAPERS.n: Preprint. Weekly panel of 23,014 acute respiratory infection cases from seven Sichuan sentinel hospitals (2024-2026); quasi-Poisson DLNMs (6-week lag) gave cumulative RRs for the 90th versus 10th percentile of each exposure with within-pathogen FDR control. Humidity-RSV was the most stable single association (RR 2.01, 1.06-3.82) but failed FDR (adjusted p 0.130) and vanished with temperature co-adjustment (RR 1.05). H. influenzae positivity fell with PM2.5 (no estimate given in the abstract); 12 of 40 estimates survived FDR. Positivity is a ratio among tested cases, not incidence, and two years of weekly data give little seasonal replication. Relevance: indirect - the PM2.5 result is a screening signal, not an effect estimate.

PAPERS.title: Comment on: Tutorial: Guidelines for implementing low-cost sensor networks for aerosol monitoring
PAPERS.short: J Aerosol Sci comment Gharibzadeh Yunesian low-cost sensor network guidelines tutorial
PAPERS.design: Metadata only: no abstract in Crossref at issue time
PAPERS.pm: Not stated (comment on low-cost sensor network guidance for aerosol monitoring)
PAPERS.endpoint: Not stated
PAPERS.n: Metadata only. A comment in the Journal of Aerosol Science on the published tutorial 'Guidelines for implementing low-cost sensor networks for aerosol monitoring'; Crossref carried no abstract at issue time and no finding is asserted here. Authors are Gharibzadeh and Yunesian. The content of the comment and any reply is unknown from the metadata, so it cannot be said which recommendations of the tutorial it disputes or extends. Relevance: direct - any challenge to consensus guidance on deployment, co-location and QA of low-cost aerosol networks bears on how this watch grades sensor studies; to be re-checked when full text is accessible.

PAPERS.title: Associations of Visual Landscape Quantity versus Configuration with Air Pollution along Urban Streets: A Case Study of Xuzhou, China
PAPERS.short: Atmos Pollut Res Xuzhou street view visual landscape quantity configuration air pollution
PAPERS.design: Metadata only: no abstract in Crossref at issue time
PAPERS.pm: Not stated (street-level air pollution, metric not given in metadata)
PAPERS.endpoint: Not stated
PAPERS.n: Metadata only. An Atmospheric Pollution Research case study of Xuzhou relating the quantity versus the spatial configuration of the visual street landscape to air pollution along urban streets. Crossref carried no abstract, so the pollutant, measurement method (fixed, mobile or sensor-based) and any effect size are unknown and no finding is asserted. Relevance: possibly direct - street-view landscape features are increasingly used as predictors in hyperlocal exposure models fed by mobile or low-cost sensor data; whether this study measured PM, and how, needs the full text.

PAPERS.title: Simulating PM2.5 along the trajectory to Southern Taiwan under the northeast monsoon
PAPERS.short: Atmos Res southern Taiwan northeast monsoon PM2.5 trajectory simulation long-range transport
PAPERS.design: Metadata only: no abstract in Crossref at issue time
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 (simulated along transport trajectories)
PAPERS.endpoint: Not stated
PAPERS.n: Metadata only. An Atmospheric Research paper simulating PM2.5 along the transport pathway into southern Taiwan under the winter northeast monsoon. Crossref carried no abstract; the model, evaluation data and any source attribution are unknown and no finding is asserted. Relevance: indirect - transported PM in the monsoon season changes aerosol composition and hygroscopicity, the conditions under which optical low-cost sensor calibrations built on local sources tend to drift.

PAPERS.title: Estimating PM2.5 Concentration in Ho Chi Minh City Using Sentinel-5P and Machine Learning on Google Earth Engine (GEE).
PAPERS.short: HCMUT Ho Chi Minh City Sentinel-5P ERA5 MODIS GEE XGBoost PM2.5 R2 0.784 four stations
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 estimated from Sentinel-5P, ERA5 and MODIS predictors trained on four certified stations
PAPERS.endpoint: Predictive skill (R2, MAE); annual mean PM2.5 surface
PAPERS.affil: Ho Chi Minh City University of Technology, Viet Nam; Ho Chi Minh City University of Technology, Viet Nam
PAPERS.n: Ho Chi Minh City has four certified PM2.5 stations. Sentinel-5P composition products, ERA5 meteorology and MODIS-derived parameters were combined in Google Earth Engine and four learners compared; XGBoost performed best (R2 0.784, MAE 2.53 ug/m3), giving a citywide annual mean of 21.55 +/- 0.92 ug/m3, about 4.3 times the WHO guideline. With four training stations the validation scheme matters more than the learner; the abstract does not say whether it was spatially held out, so R2 may reflect temporal rather than spatial skill, and the tight +/-0.92 spread suggests a smooth surface. Relevance: direct - the textbook case where a dense low-cost network would supply the spatial training data four reference stations cannot.

PAPERS.title: Urban environment and socioeconomic inequalities in childhood excess weight: a cross-sectional study in Geneva, Switzerland.
PAPERS.short: Geneva children adolescents excess weight household finances PM2.5 NO2 noise greenness mediation moderation
PAPERS.pm: Residential PM2.5 and NO2 at geocoded address (model not stated in abstract)
PAPERS.endpoint: Parent-reported excess weight (overweight or obesity)
PAPERS.affil: Geneva University Hospitals, Switzerland
PAPERS.n: Population sample of 1,006 children (2-9 y) and 1,154 adolescents (10-17 y) in Geneva. Among children, average-to-poor household finances raised odds of excess weight (aOR 1.79, 1.13-2.84) and daytime and night-time noise were associated with it (aOR 1.40, 1.10-1.77; 1.37, 1.08-1.74). PM2.5 was not associated on its own; the financial situation x PM2.5 interaction was aOR 1.59 (0.98-2.59), suggestive but null. No associations in adolescents. Height and weight were parent-reported, the design is cross-sectional, and the PM2.5 increment is not stated in the abstract; Geneva PM2.5 contrasts are narrow and collinear with NO2 and noise. Relevance: indirect - modelled residential PM; no sensor content.

PAPERS.title: Yellow dust induces pulmonary injury via AKT/Nrf2 inhibition mediated by oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction in alveolar macrophages.
PAPERS.short: Korea Institute of Toxicology yellow dust BALB/c MH-S alveolar macrophage AKT Nrf2 mitochondrial ROS
PAPERS.pm: Yellow (Asian) dust instilled in mice and applied to MH-S macrophages; dose not stated in abstract
PAPERS.endpoint: Lung inflammation, mitochondrial function, ROS, AKT/Nrf2 signalling, cell death
PAPERS.affil: Korea Institute of Toxicology, Republic of Korea; Korea Institute of Toxicology, Republic of Korea
PAPERS.n: Yellow dust instilled in male BALB/c mice produced inflammatory infiltration with pigment-laden alveolar macrophages and cytokine release. In MH-S macrophages dust depolarised mitochondria, lowered ATP, raised ROS and lipid peroxidation, increased SOD2 and GPX1 but decreased SOD1 and catalase, inhibited AKT phosphorylation and Nrf2 nuclear translocation and caused necrotic-type death; an ROS inhibitor attenuated ROS, cell death and LDH release. Dose, particle size distribution and dust provenance are not given in the abstract, and instillation bypasses deposition physics. Relevance: indirect - mechanistic arm for mineral dust, the coarse fraction optical low-cost sensors under-read.

PAPERS.title: How air pollution, Saharan dust and biomass combustion affect the heatwave threshold definition and mortality in Madrid (Spain).
PAPERS.short: ISCIII Madrid heatwave threshold air pollution Saharan dust biomass combustion mortality 2014-2023 overestimate 27.7%
PAPERS.pm: Daily PM10 and PM2.5 with NO2 and O3 from monitors (network not stated in abstract)
PAPERS.endpoint: Heatwave definition temperature; daily all-cause mortality attributable to heat and pollution
PAPERS.affil: Carlos III Health Institute, Spain; Carlos III Health Institute, Spain
PAPERS.n: Madrid daily all-cause mortality 2014-2023 with maximum temperature and NO2, O3, PM10 and PM2.5. Mortality anomalies were prewhitened without and with pollution to locate the heatwave threshold temperature. Accounting for pollution moved the threshold from 36.7 to 37.4 C, implying heatwave mortality is overestimated by 27.7% when pollution is ignored. Saharan dust intrusion and biomass-burning days raised all four pollutants. No CI is given for the threshold shift or the 27.7%, a single city is analysed, and prewhitening-based threshold estimation is sensitive to the smoothing choices. Relevance: indirect - heat-pollution attribution depends on monitor-level PM on dust days, when optical sensors are least accurate.

PAPERS.title: Effects of Cooking With Liquefied Petroleum Gas or Biomass on Lung Function Among Pre-School Aged Children in Peru: A Prospective Follow-Up of a Randomized Trial.
PAPERS.short: HAPIN Peru LPG vs biomass RCT follow-up oscillometry 3-5 year olds R7 X7 AX7 PM2.5 CO
PAPERS.pm: Prenatal and postnatal personal PM2.5 and CO exposure from the trial's monitoring
PAPERS.endpoint: Oscillometric lung function z-scores (R7, X7, fres, AX7) at age 3-5
PAPERS.affil: Johns Hopkins University, USA; Johns Hopkins University, USA
PAPERS.n: Follow-up of 101 children aged 3-5 whose mothers were randomised to LPG stoves or usual biomass during pregnancy and infancy (HAPIN Peru). Oscillometry z-scores did not differ by arm (e.g. R7 -0.1 vs -0.2; AX7 1.2 vs 1.3); the only difference was a larger post-bronchodilator fall in fres z-score with LPG (-0.36, -0.71 to -0.02). No exposure-response association was found for prenatal or postnatal PM2.5; postnatal CO was associated with worse reactance (AX7 +0.041 z per 1 ppm, 0.003-0.078). Small subsample of the trial, many endpoints, and the CO signal is exploratory. Relevance: direct - a randomised exposure contrast with personal monitoring that still found no PM2.5 lung-function gradient in early childhood.

PAPERS.title: Home sweet home-a breath full of fresh air or a lungful of woes: A cross-sectional study to explore determinants of indoor air pollution and factors influencing the use of unclean fuels.
PAPERS.short: Ahmedabad urban slum household air pollution biomass 47.1% PMUY uptake 16.7% mosquito coil incense
PAPERS.pm: No PM measured; household fuel and indoor combustion sources by interview
PAPERS.endpoint: Prevalence of indoor combustion sources; PMUY LPG scheme awareness and uptake; respiratory symptoms
PAPERS.affil: B. J. Medical College, India; Christian Medical College and Hospital, India
PAPERS.n: Community survey of 139 households in three urban slums in western India. Biomass fuel was used in 47.1% of households, often alongside indoor smoking, mosquito coils and incense; ventilation was poor and separate kitchens and exhausts rare. 80.4% knew of the PMUY clean-cooking scheme but only 16.7% had used it. No household variable predicted unclean fuel use in multivariable models and CIs were wide. No pollutant was measured, symptoms were self-reported, and the sample was powered for fuel prevalence, not for association. Relevance: indirect - documents stacked indoor sources (coils, incense, biomass) that a single kitchen PM sensor would integrate but not apportion.

PAPERS.title: Wood smoke fire particulate matter induces eosinophilic asthma in a Sprouty2-dependent manner in mice.
PAPERS.short: National Jewish Health wood smoke PM mouse eosinophilic asthma Sprouty2 deletion ILC2 ERK1/2 IL-13
PAPERS.pm: Wood smoke particulate matter by airway exposure; dose not stated in abstract
PAPERS.endpoint: Airway hyperreactivity, eosinophilic/neutrophilic inflammation, mucus, remodelling; ILC2 and Th cytokines
PAPERS.affil: National Jewish Health, USA; National Jewish Health, USA
PAPERS.n: Short-term airway exposure of naive B6 mice to wood smoke PM induced methacholine hyperreactivity, eosinophilic and modest neutrophilic inflammation, mucus production and remodelling, with more ILC2s and CD4 T cells, ERK1/2 phosphorylation and IL-5, IL-13 and IL-17A. Inducible Spry2 deletion prevented hyperreactivity, inflammation, mucus, collagen deposition and ERK1/2 activation, reduced ILC2 (not CD4 T cell) expansion and cut IL-13 and IL-17A. Dose, particle generation and group sizes are not in the abstract; acute dosing in naive mice models an exposure pattern, not chronic ambient smoke. Relevance: indirect - mechanism behind wildfire-smoke asthma, the exposure most commonly tracked with PurpleAir networks.
